context.title: Tell the Next Generation
context.summary: Asaph retells Israel's history from Egypt to David as a lesson for children: God kept doing wonders, Israel kept forgetting and rebelling, and still God chose Judah, Zion and David the shepherd.
context.background: Title: 'Maschil of Asaph.' A historical psalm and, at 72 verses, the second longest psalm. It explains why leadership passed from Ephraim (and the sanctuary at Shiloh) to Judah and Jerusalem. Matthew 13:35 cites verse 2 about Jesus' parables.

customs.note: Zoan (Tanis) was a major city in Egypt's Nile Delta (Numbers 13:22).
Literally 'bread of the mighty,' a poetic name for manna.

watchFor: The cycle repeats: wonders, forgetting, judgment, mercy.
David chosen 'from the sheepfolds' to shepherd Israel (vv. 70–72).

w: and he made to stand up
and he made to flow down
and he brought to an end
and they provoked to anger him

people.name: Asaph
people.summary: A Levite; one of the leaders of David’s choir (1 Chr. 6:39). Psalms 50 and 73-83 inclusive are attributed to him. He is mentioned along with David as skilled in music, and a “seer” (2 Chr. 29:30).

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Ephraim
people.summary: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20).

people.name: Ham
people.summary: Warm, hot, and hence the south; also an Egyptian word meaning “black”, the youngest son of Noah (Gen. 5:32; comp. 9:22, 24).

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 30:23, 24), who, on the occasion of his birth, said, “God hath taken away [Heb. ‘asaph] my reproach.”

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Zoan
places.summary: (Old Egypt. Sant= “stronghold,” the modern San). A city on the Tanitic branch of the Nile, called by the Greeks Tanis.

places.name: Shiloh
places.summary: Generally understood as denoting the Messiah, “the peaceful one,” as the word signifies (Gen. 49:10). The Vulgate Version translates the word, “he who is to be sent,” in allusion to the Messiah; the Revised Version, margin, “till he come to Shiloh;” and the LXX., “until that which is his shall come to Shiloh.”

places.name: mount Zion
places.summary: Sunny; height, one of the eminences on which Jerusalem was built. It was surrounded on all sides, except the north, by deep valleys, that of the Tyropoeon separating it from Moriah, which it surpasses in height by 105 feet.
